name: Comparative Failure Pattern Analysis
prompt:
You are given descriptions of two fictional security/infrastructure failures. Analyze both and produce a comparative report. Do not fetch any external URLs.

Failure A — Database Credential Leak:
A startup called DataPipe accidentally committed AWS credentials to a public GitHub repository on 2024-01-10 at 14:00 UTC. A bot scanned the repo and used the credentials to spin up EC2 instances for crypto mining within 3 minutes (14:03 UTC). The team discovered the mining activity via an AWS billing alert at 16:30 UTC, revoked the credentials at 16:45 UTC, and terminated rogue instances by 17:00 UTC. 120,000 dollars of unauthorized AWS charges were incurred.

Failure B — Database Injection Outage:
A web app called ShopEasy had a SQL injection vulnerability introduced in a deployment on 2024-02-20 at 10:00 UTC. An attacker discovered and exploited it at 11:30 UTC, dumping 50,000 user records. The company's WAF detected anomalous query patterns at 11:45 UTC. The vulnerable endpoint was taken offline at 12:00 UTC. A patch was deployed at 14:00 UTC and the endpoint restored.

Produce a file named comparison_report.json with this exact structure:
{
  "failures": [
    {
      "id": "A",
      "name": "DataPipe Credential Leak",
      "type": "...",
      "mttd_minutes": <int>,
      "mttr_minutes": <int>,
      "financial_impact": "...",
      "data_impact": "...",
      "root_cause_category": "...",
      "key_vulnerabilities": ["...", "..."]
    },
    { "id": "B", ... }
  ],
  "common_patterns": ["..."],
  "key_differences": ["..."],
  "priority_recommendation": "..."
}
mttd = time from incident start to detection. mttr = time from detection to full restoration. Include at least 2 items each in key_vulnerabilities, common_patterns, and key_differences.

criteria.description: comparison_report.json file is present in the workspace.
comparison_report.json contains all four required top-level keys: failures, common_patterns, key_differences, and priority_recommendation.
The failures array contains exactly 2 entries.
Each failure object has the fields id, name, mttd_minutes, mttr_minutes, root_cause_category, and key_vulnerabilities.
The two failure id values are exactly "A" and "B".
criteria.testPattern: failure IDs are A and B

criteria.description: mttd_minutes and mttr_minutes for each failure are positive numeric values greater than zero.
Failure A mttd_minutes is approximately 150 (within ±10), matching the 14:00–16:30 detection window.
Each failure's key_vulnerabilities array has at least 2 entries.
The top-level common_patterns array has at least 2 entries identifying shared patterns across both failures.
The top-level key_differences array has at least 2 entries distinguishing the two failures.

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent analyzed two fictional failures and produced a comparative JSON report.

Criterion 1: Metric Accuracy (Weight: 50%)
1.0: Failure A mttd=150 min (14:00 to 16:30), mttr=30 min (16:30 to 17:00); Failure B mttd=75 min (10:00 to 11:15 exploit + WAF at 11:45 = 105 min from deployment, or 15 min from exploit), mttr=75 min (11:45 to 14:00) — reasonable interpretation of the timeline is accepted with ±5 min tolerance.
0.5: One failure has a metric off by more than 10 minutes.
0: Multiple metrics are significantly wrong.

Criterion 2: Comparative Insight Quality (Weight: 50%)
1.0: common_patterns identify shared issues (both involve lack of preventative controls, rapid attacker exploitation), key_differences correctly identify distinct aspects (credential vs code vulnerability, financial vs data impact), priority_recommendation is specific and actionable.
0.5: Patterns/differences are generic without connecting to specifics of these two incidents.
0: Comparative sections are superficial or copy the incident descriptions verbatim.
eval.name: Quality Judge
